title: [CQ-I06c] Test-free packaged helper bundles
definitionOfDone: A fresh daemon build no longer emits dist/tools/toolTestHarness.js, and the daemon `npx tsc --noEmit` stays green. Both are shown in a Linux snapshot build.

The actual VS Code bundler run in local-runner-bundle.test.mjs copies vm-control.mjs byte-identical and refuses to bundle without it. A *.test.* or *.spec.* file planted in either dist is absent from the bundle, while dist/index.js is still copied.

The onboarding packaged checks, run by the bundle test against real bundler output, pass on the clean bundle. They refuse a missing vm-control.mjs, a vm-control.mjs whose import closure is broken, and a test artifact under daemon/, proxy/ or scripts/. A test file inside node_modules is ignored.
The static Gradle checks in the same test pin that requireBundledAssets names vm-control.mjs, and that the daemon and proxy dist copies exclude **/*.test.* and **/*.spec.*.
Fresh `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs` exits 0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: Packaging only: never change what a production module does at runtime; never remove an asset a wrapper or IDE loads by path.

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST (RED). Load test-driven-development. Edit only scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs. It runs the ACTUAL moe-vscode bundler in a temp repo (fixture()) and slices scripts/tests/onboarding.mjs up to `const require = createRequire(proxyEntry);` to get its packaged checks.

Fixture and list changes:
- Add 'vm-control.mjs' to the `required` array. The existing byte-identity test and the onboarding missing-file loop then cover it.
- In fixture(), also plant compiled-test files in the fake dists: packages/moe-proxy/dist/index.test.js, packages/moe-proxy/dist/index.test.d.ts, packages/moe-proxy/dist/utils.spec.js and packages/moe-daemon/dist/tools/sample.test.js. Every bundle run then exercises the filter.

New or changed tests. Assert exact statuses and paths; never assert truthiness.
- T1 'actual bundler drops compiled tests and specs from both dists': the four planted files are absent under work.output (proxy/..., daemon/tools/...), while proxy/index.js and daemon/index.js are present.
- T2: turn 'actual bundler refuses a missing required provider asset' into a loop over ['doctor.mjs', 'vm-control.mjs']. Each case expects status 1 and stderr matching /local-runner.*<name>/.
- T3 'bundled onboarding loads the packaged vm-control import closure':
  - the clean bundle passes (status 0);
  - delete output scripts/local-runner/lifecycle.mjs. It is in vm-control's closure but not in `required`. Expect status !== 0 and stderr matching /vm-control/. Restore it;
  - replace output vm-control.mjs with `process.stdout.write('{"code":"OTHER"}\n'); process.exit(2);`. Expect it to be refused, which proves stdout is checked and not only the exit code.
- T4 'bundled onboarding refuses any test artifact outside node_modules':
  - Plant each of these one at a time: daemon/tools/toolTestHarness.js, proxy/utils.test.js, scripts/local-runner/fixtures/data.json and scripts/mods/example/__tests__/x.mjs. Each must be refused, with stderr matching /test artifact/ and naming that relative path. Remove each after its case.
  - Then plant daemon/node_modules/dependency/test/a.test.js and proxy/node_modules/dep/__tests__/b.js. Status must stay 0.
- T5 (static) 'Gradle requires vm-control and drops compiled tests': read moe-jetbrains/build.gradle.kts and check three things:
  - the requireBundledAssets local-runner listOf(...) names "vm-control.mjs";
  - the `from(bundledDaemonDir) {` block contains `exclude("**/*.test.*", "**/*.spec.*")`;
  - the `from(bundledProxyDir) {` block contains the same exclude.
  Slice each block up to its closing `}` the way the existing Gradle test does.
- T6 (static) 'daemon build excludes the test-only tool harness': JSON.parse packages/moe-daemon/tsconfig.json and assert that exclude contains both 'src/**/*.test.ts' and 'src/tools/toolTestHarness.ts'.

RED: run `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs` with Linux node via `env -i` (`mem:gotcha-local-runner-tests`). T1-T6 and the vm-control onboarding-missing case must fail before step 2; record the counts in the step note. Do NOT touch the CI-regex test.

- Could the dist filter drop a production module? Grep packages/moe-daemon/src and packages/moe-proxy/src for production imports of a *.test or *.spec path. There must be none.
- Production file names that merely contain 'test' without the dots must survive, for example latest.js or attestation.js.
- The required-asset lists (taskRail) still name every asset a wrapper or IDE loads by path. JetBrains resolves scripts/local-runner/vm-control.mjs, moe-agent.ps1/.sh, daemon/index.js and proxy/index.js. VS Code resolves bundled/daemon/index.js, proxy/index.js and scripts/moe-agent.*.
- Windows: path.sep inside the filters; the relative paths in the scan message are '/'-joined; the exec uses an argument array with no shell; windowsHide is set.
- A missing bundle directory (no scripts/) must fail loudly rather than pass an empty scan.
- The node_modules skip applies only to directories named exactly node_modules.
- Running vm-control needs no network and no daemon, and touches no ledger. Usage validation comes first.
- CI: the 'Verify packaged JetBrains onboarding' step now proves the same checks against the real JetBrains zip.
- Rails: packaging only, no runtime behaviour change, no .moe edits, no Git writes, and none of globalRails.forbiddenPatterns.
Then write the Serena memory 'task-task-f18eef7acc5140cdbe6f545a7f82434d-handoff' for CQ-I06. It covers the guards, the scan rule, the mutant list, and the residual that the npm moe-proxy package still ships compiled tests.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Both IDE packages refuse to build without scripts/local-runner/vm-control.mjs. Neither copies compiled tests or specs from the daemon and proxy dists, and the daemon build stops emitting tools/toolTestHarness.js. The onboarding packaged checks prove two things against a real bundle: the packaged vm-control import closure loads (usage refusal exit 2), and no test artifact exists outside node_modules. CI's existing 'Verify packaged JetBrains onboarding' step then enforces the same rules on the real JetBrains zip.
acceptanceCriteria: T1-T6 and the vm-control onboarding-missing case in scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs fail before the change and pass after it. The mutants M1-M8 are each killed by their named test.

A real VS Code bundle built from fresh dists passes `node scripts/tests/onboarding.mjs moe-vscode/bundled`, and the test-artifact find over it prints nothing.
invariants: No production module's runtime behaviour changes.
Every asset a wrapper or IDE loads by path stays bundled and required.
The node_modules copies and their .bin exclusion are unchanged.
No .moe edits and no Git writes by the agent.
compatibility: The proxy tsconfig is unchanged, so `npm run build` still typechecks proxy tests.
The existing bundle, exclusion and onboarding tests keep passing unchanged, apart from the added 'vm-control.mjs' entry and the doctor-only refusal test that becomes a two-name loop.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Fixing the proxy at source, with a tsconfig exclude for tests: rejected. The proxy would lose build-time typechecking of its tests, because vitest does not typecheck. Bundler filters fix the packaged plugins, which is this DoD. The npm package residual is recorded for CQ-I06.
- Renaming toolTestHarness.ts: it has 89 importers, so that is too much churn. A tsconfig exclude is one line, and the daemon already excludes its tests.
- Hard-coding vm-control's whole import closure in the required lists: it would go stale. Instead the packaged usage-refusal exec proves the static closure at once, because ESM resolves every static import before running.
- Scanning node_modules too: third-party packages legitimately ship tests, so the scan skips node_modules by design.
